key_insight: Open-source thigh muscle MRI segmentation tools vary widely in performance, and task-specific models trained on large datasets performed best.
clinical_relevance: Reliable muscle segmentation can improve volumetric, radiomic, and fat-fraction analysis in neuromuscular MRI, but errors may affect interpretation in clinical and research settings.
method: Benchmarked 8 open-source segmentation tools on 3D thigh MRI.
Tested on 3 base datasets, then additional derived datasets.
Compared quantitative accuracy and qualitative usability across methods.
evidence_signal: The study found substantial performance differences across tools and datasets, with many methods losing accuracy on pathological cases.
watch_item: Results may not generalize well to underrepresented populations or uncommon pathologies, so deployment needs caution and local validation.
paper_title: Benchmarking open-source automated thigh muscle MRI segmentation algorithms
